title: The Spider: from core to add-on
description: How the ZAP Spider (the traditional crawler) is recorded in the zaproxy and zap-extensions histories, with the blog posts around it: code in core since 2012, the 2022 migration of the Spider into the spider add-on, the removal of the core code, and the .DS_Store parser.
narrative:
Crawling a site is usually one of the first steps in a scan. ZAP's traditional Spider lived in core code from 2010 until its migration in 2022. In May 2012 a new SpiderParam and Spider class were added under org.zaproxy.zap.spider, and the old Paros Proxy spider packages were removed in July 2012. An announcement in December 2012 indicates that the old spider was "showing its age", and during ZAP's first year in Google Summer of Code, Cosmin Stefan completely rewrote it.

An add-on spider with SVG href parsing followed in January 2022, and in April 2022 a migration commit moved the Spider from core to zap-extensions as core deprecated it.

An announcement in August 2022 indicates that the changes were available for testing in the weekly releases ahead of 2.12, and explained the point of the move: "the core Spider has been moved to an add-on which means such changes are no longer bound to core/stable releases." The post reported that the weekly version took ZAP from a score of 50% to 80% on Google's Security Crawl Maze, and warned that some third-party add-ons using the Spider would stop working with 2.12.

The core code was removed in January 2026, when a commit titled Remove deprecated spider deleted 22085 lines. The spider add-on's changelog lists version 0.20.0 from April 2026. As of the sources cited, the Spider is an add-on in zap-extensions, and the core spider directory no longer exists in zaproxy.

narrative_sources.label: ZAP 2.0.0 and the Google Summer of Code 2012 Projects

chapters.title: Spider code in core, 2010 to 2012
chapters.text: The commit "Version 1.0.0" (2010-09-04) adds files under src/org/parosproxy/paros/core/spider. On 2012-05-29 the commit "New SpiderParam in org.zaproxy.zap.spider. Modified extensions to accommodate with change." adds src/org/zaproxy/zap/spider/Spider.java and SpiderParam.java, and the commit "Switched to new Spider. ParosProxy implementations not used anymore." is dated the same day. On 2012-07-12 the commit "Removed old and unused Spider-related Paros Proxy packages." follows. The post "ZAP 2.0.0 and the Google Summer of Code 2012 Projects" (2012-12-10) explains why: "The current ZAP spider is showing its age." Cosmin Stefan, in ZAP's first year in Google Summer of Code, "completely rewrote the spider, which is now much faster and more comprehensive than the old one", and made it session aware.

evidence.label: ZAP 2.0.0 and the Google Summer of Code 2012 Projects

chapters.title: January 2017: Spider functionality moved within core
chapters.text: On 2017-01-02 the commit "Deprecate unused Spider menu items" is dated; on 2017-01-04 the commit "Move Spider functionality to Spider extension" is dated. Both are in zaproxy and the Spider code is still in core at that point.

chapters.title: 2022: the spider add-on and the core deprecation
chapters.text: In zap-extensions, "feat: spider: Add spider add-on with SVG href parsing" is dated 2022-01-20 and "feat: Spider Migration" is dated 2022-04-27; the latter's message says the migration of the spider from core to zap-extensions is based on an earlier zaproxy commit. About a minute later, also on 2022-04-27, zaproxy has "chore: Spider Deprecation", whose diff adds @Deprecated annotations (47 added lines match). The add-on commit "spider: Promote to Release status" is dated 2022-06-27, and zaproxy's "Include spider add-on in weeklies" is dated 2022-08-22. The post "Spider News" (2022-08-30) by Rick Mitchell announces that the changes are available for testing in the weekly releases ahead of 2.12, and explains the point of the move: "the core Spider has been moved to an add-on which means such changes are no longer bound to core/stable releases". Quick Start, Form Handler, GraphQL, OpenAPI, SOAP and the Automation Framework were reworked to use the add-on, and "Some Third Party add-ons which use the Spider will stop working with the release of 2.12." Against Google's Security Crawl Maze, "ZAP has gone from a score of 50% to 80% with the current weekly functionality", improvements the post says were mostly "a result of efforts related to Issue 7152".

chapters.title: The .DS_Store parser, 2022 to 2023
chapters.text: The Spider News post ends with future plans, including "plan to add .DS_Store file parsing". On 2023-01-20 zap-extensions has "spider: Add .DS_Store handling", and on 2023-09-21 "spider: exclude `DsStore` from JavaDoc". On 2023-09-08 the post "Parsing .DS_Store files with ZAP" by Paul-Emmanuel Raoul explains the idea: macOS .DS_Store files hold Finder metadata and, published by accident, leak a site's file hierarchy. The format was never public ("The specifications detailing the internal structure of .DS_Store files have never been made public"), so he described it for Kaitai Struct, a parser generator, and the post links the resulting DsStoreParser.java in the spider add-on. Once the Spider finds a file named .DS_Store, each file name in it becomes a URL the Spider tries. The post thanks kingthorin for working on the implementation and says "It took years from the moment I started poking around with the Kaitai Struct project".

chapters.title: 2026: the deprecated core Spider is removed
chapters.text: On 2026-01-23 zaproxy has the commit "Remove deprecated spider" (68 files changed, 22085 lines deleted). At HEAD the directory zap/src/main/java/org/zaproxy/zap/spider does not exist in zaproxy, while addOns/spider exists in zap-extensions; the spider add-on's changelog lists version 0.20.0 dated 2026-04-02.
